question.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}x\,dx+{z}^{3}\,dy-{y}^{2}\,dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the line $r(t)=\sqrt{2}t\,i+2t\,j+2t\,k$ for $t\in [1,4]?$
question.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=\sqrt{2}t,\,y(t)=2t,\,z(t)=2t.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2}t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,k \\  & =\sqrt{2}\,i+2\,j+2\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}x\,dx+{z}^{3}\,dy-{y}^{2}\,dz & ={\int }_{1}^{4}x\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+{z}^{3}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt-{y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}(x\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+{z}^{3}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}-{y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}\sqrt{2}t\cdot (\sqrt{2})+8{t}^{3}\cdot (2)-4{t}^{2}\cdot (2)\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}16{t}^{3}-8{t}^{2}+2t\,dt\end{aligned}
$$
